newsitem.title: MACEDONIA: Macedonia obtains $81 mln ESAF credit.
newsitem.headline: Macedonia obtains $81 mln ESAF credit.

text.p: Macedonia has negotiated an $81 million credit with the International Monetary Fund (IMF), a senior government official said on Thursday.

"Macedonia obtained an $81 million credit from the IMF's Enhanced Structural Adjustment Facility (ESAF)," Ljube Trpevski, minister without portfolio and head of the Macedonian negotiating team with the IMF, told a news conference.
The credit, to be paid off in 15 years, has a five-year grace period and carries an annual 0.5 percent interest, Trpevski said.
"The funds will be drawn out semi-annually during the next three years," he added.
Robert Corker, the IMF official responsible for Macedonia, said "the IMF board of Directors will approve this credit at the beginning of next year."
"This credit will help Macedonia achieve the goals of its macroeconomic policies," Macedonian Finance Minister Taki Fiti said.

Key macroeconomic targets involve up to 5 percent annual GDP growth, a reduction of the balance of payment deficit, maintenance of two percent inflation and keeping the denar foreign exchange rate stable, Fiti said.
This is the third credit approved by the IMF to Macedonia over the last two years. -- Mircela Casule, Skopje newsroom, +389 91 201 196
